skill.name: config-auditing
skill.description: Audit Neovim configurations for structural problems, deprecated APIs, security concerns, and performance issues using version-aware checklists and established Lua practices.
skill.summary: Review Neovim health, compatibility, security, and performance with structured local checks.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: This documentation skill uses read-only shell checks against local Neovim files; most static alerts misclassify examples, keymap names, and conventional paths. Two checks use predictable temporary files, and the credential scan can print plaintext secrets. Headless validation also executes the active configuration without isolation.

remediation.issue: The credential detection command prints complete matching lines, including possible secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Report only file names and line numbers, or redact assignment values before any result enters agent context.

remediation.issue: Headless checks load and sometimes explicitly execute the active Neovim configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated configuration for passive checks and require explicit consent before executing the target configuration.

remediation.issue: Startup checks write to predictable shared paths under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary file securely, restrict its permissions, and remove it immediately after reading.

content.value_statement: Neovim configurations can hide deprecated APIs, security issues, and startup bottlenecks. This skill provides structured checks, version guidance, and practical recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Neovim configuration structure and modular organization.
Identifies documented deprecated APIs for Neovim versions 0.9 through 0.12.
Checks common security concerns, including hardcoded credentials and unsafe shell construction.
Evaluates lazy.nvim loading patterns and likely startup bottlenecks.
Recommends modern Lua option, keymap, and autocmd patterns.
limitations: Deprecation guidance may become outdated as Neovim releases change.
Static patterns can produce false positives and require human review.
Startup measurements depend on the local machine, plugins, and cache state.
The included commands do not safely isolate untrusted Neovim configurations.

use_cases.title: Review a personal configuration
use_cases.description: Find structural, compatibility, and security issues before upgrading Neovim.

use_cases.title: Modernize shared editor settings
use_cases.description: Replace deprecated APIs and standardize Lua patterns across a maintained configuration.

use_cases.title: Investigate slow startup
use_cases.description: Identify eager plugin loading, frequent autocmds, and settings that may delay startup.

prompt_templates.title: Review configuration structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Neovim configuration files. Identify structure issues and explain each recommendation without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a personal configuration

prompt_templates.title: Check deprecated APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Neovim configuration for deprecated APIs. Use version [VERSION], cite file paths and lines, and suggest supported replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Assess startup performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess startup performance using existing logs and configuration files. Rank eager plugins, top-level requires, and frequent autocmds by likely impact.

prompt_templates.title: Run a constrained security audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [CONFIG_PATH] for security and compatibility with Neovim [VERSION]. Do not execute configuration code. Redact secrets and prioritize findings by impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an unfamiliar configuration

output_examples.input: Audit my Neovim 0.10 configuration for deprecated option APIs.
output: Warning: A deprecated buffer option setter appears in lua/config/options.lua.

output_examples.input: Explain why my Neovim startup is slow.
output_examples.output: The report ranks eager plugin loads, startup autocmds, and top-level requires, then recommends targeted lazy-loading changes.

output_examples.input: Review my keymaps and configuration organization.
output: Duplicate mappings are grouped by key and source location.
Organization advice separates options, keymaps, autocmds, and plugin specifications.

best_practices: Confirm the installed Neovim version before applying version-specific deprecation guidance.
Review every shell command before execution, especially commands that load the active configuration.
Redact credential values and share only the minimum files needed for analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every deprecated API as removed without checking the target version.
Do not execute an unfamiliar Neovim configuration merely to collect audit data.
Do not paste secrets or complete private configuration trees into prompts.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my Neovim configuration?
faq.answer: No. Its documented workflow analyzes files and recommends changes, but users should review every suggested command.

faq.question: Which Neovim versions does it cover?
faq.answer: The included reference covers selected deprecations from versions 0.9 through 0.12 nightly.

faq.question: Which plugin managers are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance focuses on lazy.nvim and includes migration references for legacy packer.nvim configurations.

faq.question: Can the checks execute my configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. Some headless commands load the active configuration, so review and approve them before use.

faq.question: How should detected credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Do not share credential values. Redact matches, rotate exposed secrets, and move credentials into protected environment variables.

faq.question: Does the audit require internet access?
faq.answer: The reference checks are local, but loaded configurations or plugins may perform network operations.
